source.title_on_document: The Effects of Generative AI Use on University Students' Creative Idea Generation: Switching Effects in Repeated Task Performance (Korean title: 생성형 AI 활용이 대학생의 창의적 아이디어 생성에 미치는 영향: 동일 과제 반복 수행에서의 사용 전환 효과)

supplement.holds: The paper refers to no supplement or online appendix. All statistics (Tables 1-4, mixed-model contrasts) are in the main text.

paper_design_summary: In a classroom session, 164 students from two Korean universities wrote up to 10 ideas for the task 'Imagining an Idea That Will Change the Future in 2035' in 10 minutes, either with generative AI (group A, ChatGPT free plan by default) or without it (group B); after a 30-minute break with a YouTube video they revised and refined their ideas for another 10 minutes. For round 2, students were randomly split within each round-1 group: A kept AI (A1) or lost it (A2), B gained AI (B1) or stayed without it (B2). Two blind raters scored each idea on a four-dimension rubric (novelty, usefulness/feasibility, elaboration/specificity, future-change fit), summed to a 0-100 total per participant per round.

studies.label: Classroom experiment: two-round idea generation with AI-use switching (A1/A2/B1/B2)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Round-2 AI condition, assigned at random within each round-1 group: within A (AI in round 1), keep AI (A1) or discontinue AI (A2); within B (no AI in round 1), adopt AI (B1) or continue without AI (B2). The paper does not state how students were assigned to round-1 groups A and B (random or otherwise).
assignment.quote: 2차에서는 1차 집단(A/B) 내부에서 무작위로 전환 조건을 분기하여 A는 AI 유지(A1) 또는 AI 중단(A2), B는 AI 도입(B1) 또는 미사용 유지(B2)로 배정한다.

participants.exclusions: Only participants who completed both the round-1 and round-2 outputs were included in the analysis. The paper does not state how many students started or were excluded.
participants.who: Students at two domestic (Korean) universities taking IT-related courses; 121 men, 43 women; year and major not collected.
participants.country: South Korea (two domestic universities; Korean-language journal)
participants.quote: 분석에 포함된 참여자는 총 164명이며, 1차 조건은 A 83명, B 81명으로 구성되었다. 2차 조건은 A1 43명, A2 40명, B1 41명, B2 40명이다.
participants.locator: PDF p. 5 (journal p. 44), Section 3.1; repeated PDF p. 6 (journal p. 45), Section 4.1; Figure 1, PDF p. 4 (journal p. 43)

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT (Free plan, the default version available at the time); participants could also use other generative AI tools if they wished
ai_tool.how_used: In AI conditions students were directed to ChatGPT by default and could use other generative AI tools; usage behavior (time, prompts, purpose) was not measured (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1; PDF p. 9, Section 5.2).

task.description: 'Imagining an Idea That Will Change the Future in 2035': propose ideas (software, product, service, policy, unrestricted) that could improve life given future social changes (climate change, aging, urban crowding, mental health, relationships); up to 10 ideas per round. Round 1: produce as many diverse ideas as possible. Round 2: upgrade the round-1 output (revise, supplement, elaborate, or add new perspectives).
task.duration: Round 1: 10 minutes; break of about 30 minutes with a YouTube video; round 2: 10 minutes; all in one session

outcomes.name: Round-1 total creativity score (0-100), group A vs group B (H1)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two independent raters blind to condition scored each idea on four dimensions (novelty, usefulness/feasibility, elaboration/specificity, future-change fit), converted to a 0-10 idea score with within-round penalties of 1-3 points on novelty for similar or duplicate ideas; participant total = sum of up to 10 idea scores (0-100), averaged over the two raters. Total therefore reflects both quantity and quality (mean ideas: 9.18 round 1, 9.52 round 2). ICC for total score, round 1: single .918, average .957. Rater expertise not stated (coded human_raters).

contrasts.reported: A 63.07 (SD=15.27, n=83) vs B 29.65 (SD=16.88, n=81); Welch t(159.54)=13.29, p<.001; mean difference 33.42, 95% CI [28.45, 38.38]; Cohen's d=2.08. Note: the paper does not state that assignment to A vs B was random. (mean_difference_se listed because the mean difference and CI are printed; no SE is printed.)
contrasts.locator: PDF pp. 6-7 (journal pp. 45-46), Section 4.2; arm-level round-1 means also in Table 4, PDF p. 7 (journal p. 46)

outcomes.name: Change in total creativity score from round 1 to round 2 (round-2 revision with vs without AI), planned contrasts in mixed model (H3, H4)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same rubric total (0-100) as S1-O1, averaged over two blind raters; round-2 ICC single .920, average .958; dimension-level ICC over all 328 outputs: novelty .921, usefulness/feasibility .929, elaboration/specificity .912, future-change fit .848. Analysis: linear mixed model score ~ time x group_2 + (1 | person), reference A1, planned contrasts on the time x group interaction (the paper calls this the main analysis). Within-arm paired t-tests of the change are in Table 3.
outcomes.delay: Round 2 follows round 1 after about 30 minutes in the same session

contrasts.locator: Mixed-model contrast: PDF pp. 7-8 (journal pp. 46-47), Section 4.4.2 item 1; Table 4, PDF p. 7 (journal p. 46); Table 1, PDF p. 6 (journal p. 45)
Mixed-model contrast: PDF p. 8 (journal p. 47), Section 4.4.2 item 2; Table 4, PDF p. 7 (journal p. 46); Table 1, PDF p. 6 (journal p. 45)

outcomes.name: Round-2 total creativity score produced without AI: after AI use in round 1 (A2) vs never AI (B2)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same rubric total (0-100) as S1-O1. The paper does not test this contrast; only the arm descriptive statistics in Table 4 are printed. A2's round-2 output is a revision of its own AI-assisted round-1 draft, so the level difference mostly carries over from round 1. The A vs B split is not stated to be random.
outcomes.delay: About 30 minutes after the round-1 (AI) session, same session

contrasts.reported: Table 4 round 2: A2 64.65 (SD 15.08, n=40) vs B2 38.03 (SD 15.18, n=40); changes 2.50 (4.21) vs 9.10 (8.45). No test of A2 vs B2 is reported.

eligibility.reason: Within round-1 group B, students were randomly assigned to adopt AI for the round-2 revision (B1, n=41) or continue without AI (B2, n=40): 81 people analyzed, a no-AI comparison group, and a rubric creativity score from two blind raters (PDF p. 5 Section 3.1; Table 4 p. 7). A1 vs A2 (83 people) is also randomized. The round-1 A vs B contrast (H1) relies on an assignment the paper does not call random. Number randomized and attrition are not stated (only completers analyzed).

one_line_finding: Students randomly given AI for the revision round raised their 0-100 rubric creativity score by 28.63 points more than those kept without AI (SE 2.49, 95% CI [23.74, 33.52]), and removing AI cut the gain by 5.50 points (SE 2.47, p=.026) (PDF pp. 7-8, Section 4.4.2; Table 4); in round 1, AI users scored 63.07 vs 29.65 (d=2.08, Section 4.2).
open_questions: Was the round-1 assignment to A (AI) vs B (no AI) random? The paper states randomization only for the round-2 split within A and within B. H1 (S1-O1) is not a randomized contrast unless this is confirmed.
Unit of randomization for the round-2 split is not stated explicitly; individual assignment is implied by the arm counts and the individual unit of analysis.
How many students began the task, and how many were dropped for not completing both rounds?
Rater expertise is not described ('2명의 독립 평가자'); coded human_raters, could be expert_raters.
Design class: a single supervised class session inside IT courses ('실제 수업 맥락에서 수행한 교육 현장 실험'); coded field_rct, could be read as lab_rct.
The total score sums up to 10 idea scores, so it mixes quantity and quality; the paper notes it cannot fully separate them (PDF p. 5, Section 3.2.2; PDF p. 9, Section 5.2).
notes: Locators give PDF page (1-10) and journal page (40-49); PDF page N = journal page 39+N. No diversity or similarity outcome is measured. Other printed results not coded as contrasts: H2 pooled within-person change, round 1 46.57 (SD 23.19) to round 2 60.93 (SD 19.66), paired t(163)=10.34, p<.001, mean change 14.36, 95% CI [11.62, 17.10], dz=0.81 (Table 2 and Section 4.3, PDF p. 7); Table 3 within-arm paired t-tests of the change: A1 8.00 [5.57, 10.43] dz 1.01, A2 2.50 [1.15, 3.85] dz 0.59, B1 37.73 [31.71, 43.75] dz 1.98, B2 9.10 [6.40, 11.80] dz 1.08; H5 asymmetry contrast (B1-B2) - (A1-A2): estimate=23.13, SE=3.51, z=6.60, p<.001, 95% CI [16.26, 30.00] (PDF p. 8, Section 4.4.2 item 3). Mixed-model time effect for reference A1: 8.00, SE=1.71, z=4.68, p<.001, 95% CI [4.65, 11.35]. The B1 vs B2 contrast is the cleanest randomized AI-vs-no-AI estimate; note that the round-2 output of B1 is an AI-assisted revision of an unassisted draft. The mixed-model SEs are on participant-level scores (random intercept per person).
